newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Mexico 1997 GDP growth seen at 4.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Mexico 1997 GDP growth seen at 4.7 pct.

text.p: ING Barings said on Monday it had increased its estimate on growth in Mexico's real gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 to 4.7 percent from its previously forecast 4.0 percent.
The company said that it had maintained its GDP growth forecast for 1998 unchanged at 5.5 percent.
ING Barings said that Mexico is expected to enjoy increasingly dynamic GDP growth in 1997 with exports, investment and consumption taking turns leading economic expansion.

Investment is expected to contribute more to GDP growth than consumption and the net external sector in 1997, and is likely to return to pre-1994 levels in less than three years, ING Barings' Mexico economist Sergio Martn said in the report.
"Consumption recovery has been slow, but signs of improvement in employment and real wage growth show that a solid recovery in this sector is possible by 1998," ING Barings said.
Exports are also seen losing momentum in 1997 and into 1998, it said.
